paragraphs: The Vario 614D/615D uses either the OM612 or OM647 — both diesel engines fitted across the 1996–2013 production run. These engines are shared with the equivalent-era Sprinter, which is why the known wear pattern is so well documented. Both codes are 2.2L to 2.7L units, and both share the same vulnerability to timing chain and gear wear, along with injector seal failure. Which one your particular van has depends on the exact build specification and year, which is why we always confirm by registration before quoting. The Vario 614D/615D is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every VARIO 614D 615D on the road.

cards.body: A diesel unit fitted to the Vario 614D/615D from 1996 to 2013. Known for timing chain and gear wear, along with injector seal failure over time — shared pattern with the equivalent-era Sprinter. We replace timing chain components, timing gears, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every OM612 rebuild.

A diesel unit fitted to the Vario 614D/615D from 1996 to 2013. Shares the same known wear pattern as the OM612 — timing chain and gear wear, plus injector seal failure. We replace the same components — timing chain, timing gears, injector seals and gaskets — as standard on every OM647 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the Vario 614D/615D spans two confirmed engine codes across the same production window, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming parts from one will work on the other without checking — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Vario quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
